title: About — ScrumIA
meta_description: Where ScrumIA comes from, what it borrows from BMAD, and what it deliberately does not claim.
heading: About
page_lead: Where ScrumIA comes from, the premise it runs on, and what it deliberately leaves for you to decide.
origin_p1: ScrumIA comes out of six months building with Claude Code and BMAD, on personal projects. It is maintained by tibs245.
origin_p2: BMAD supplied the foundations that are still here: a modular base, versioned installs, and tooling kept separate from the projects that consume it.
premise_p1: There is no single right way to run a project with an AI. What works on a five-app monorepo doesn't work on a personal script; what suits a regulated team doesn't suit a weekend prototype.
premise_p2: A method that answers every question at once has to be taken whole or left. In practice it gets taken, adapted, drifts, and ends as a fork that stops receiving updates.
premise_p3: ScrumIA separates the questions and gives each one a replaceable module. The reusable part is the composition, not the answers put into it.
claims_li1: That these boundaries between slots are the right ones for everyone
claims_li2: That a per-feature file catalogue beats other spec formats
claims_li3: That this set of roles is the right one
claims_li4: That state must live outside the repository
claims_note: Each of those is a choice made for a context, documented with its alternatives in the architecture decision records. A module-level decision is contested by writing another module, not by arguing about this one.
status_r6_state: Not yet — a pilot is next
status_note_title: The real test of the architecture
status_note_p: As long as a single module fills a slot, nothing proves that slot is genuinely replaceable. Writing a second tracker module — even a minimal file-based one — would tell us more than adding another implementation module.
related_rex_p: A slide deck on lessons learned with Claude Code and the model family — divide and conquer, sub-agents, right-sizing models. Same author.
related_bmad_p: The full-lifecycle framework ScrumIA borrows its modular base from. Broader in scope and supports several tools.
license_p: MIT. Fork it, strip it down, replace the modules that don't suit you.
